first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ—both point directly to friction in the early user experience. Memory_31 and memory_86 demonstrated that signup simplification and onboarding optimization produce durable activation and completion lifts. I'm verifying these two to confirm the magnitude and durability of prior gains before running a similar simplification experiment. This directly addresses the activation and onboarding completion declines without cannibilizing long-term revenue (unlike promotional pricing, which could devalue the product for price-sensitive segments and weaken positioning against the competitor). Referral incentives and sales assist target different segments and won't resolve the QoQ activation decline. A standard experiment allows us to measure whether the prior gains replicate in the current cohort and competitive environment, while preserving ability to scale if results hold.
